_why: This repository's lanes: the domains inside it that work is dispatched to, each owning its paths (D115, docs/2026-10-01-self-development-design.md §2.1; the map of docs/2026-09-30-parallel-development-design.md §5, which a test holds to this file by id and title). Today tools/merge-branch.mjs reads it, prints which lanes a branch touched, and never refuses a merge on it; the driver, its queue and `connect` are to read it as DEV4 to DEV6 land. `id` is how work addresses a lane: lower-case letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter, unique here. `title` and `summary` are for the people and agents that address it. A path belongs to the first lane that owns it, the steward's before the rest. `steward` marks the one lane that keeps the records, which a lane session never edits. `gates` names the declared gates a landing of that lane alone needs; absent is every gate, only the steward's narrows, and the merge tool runs every gate whatever a branch touched. `laneless` lists what belongs to no lane on purpose, each group with its reason; a test refuses a tracked file that is in no lane and not listed there, so a new path is placed when it is added, never left outside silently (LEFT1). A repeated or malformed id, a lane with no paths, two stewards, or a gate nobody declared makes the file unreadable. Globs: `*` stays inside one folder, `**` crosses folders, `{a,b}` is either, and a path starting `!` carves a narrower lane's files out of a wider one.

lanes.title: Web shell
lanes.summary: The page but its Settings: the frame, the bridge, the atoms, the work frame, every other screen, the modules they share, the catalogues outside Settings' areas, and the page's build and end-to-end suite.

lanes.title: Web settings
lanes.summary: The Settings screen: its frame, one file per domain, and its catalogue areas.

lanes.title: Driver library
lanes.summary: The driver library, its headless host and their tests: the loop and planner, trees and landing, plugins and hooks, help, the toolchain.

lanes.title: Desktop modules
lanes.summary: The modules the page talks to, the application, the launcher that starts it, and the desktop tree's package versions.
lanes._why: The launcher (D93) is a twin of the modules' taskbar identity (D108). The desktop tree's package versions are the kit the application and the modules run on; the driver has no package of its own.

lanes.title: Service
lanes.summary: The cross-repository knowledge service, whole: its core, its hosts and its tests.

lanes.title: CLI
lanes.summary: The npm package daoris, whole: its sources, its entry point and its tests.

lanes.title: Tools
lanes.summary: This repository's own tooling and gates: tools/, the devkit, the gates' declaration and the release workflow that runs them, and the workspace's scripts and ignore rules.
lanes._why: The desktop suites' Process settings are here because the gates name them (MOD8). The records were this lane's until DEV2 gave them a lane of their own.

lanes.title: Records
lanes.summary: The backlog, its archive, and this map: the steward's records, which a lane session never edits.
lanes._why: The steward's lane (D115 §5), holding what the parent's list held and the map itself. The parent keeps them as the steward until a steward session does (DEV9). A landing of this lane alone needs the universal gates, which scan and link-check its files, and the cli gate, whose verify reads them: the budgets, the duplicate check and the lanes test.

laneless.what: The docs: read by every lane and written by the change that makes them stale. The steward's archive is carved out: it is the records lane's.
The doctrine and what it is synced into: a canon change re-syncs this repository's own copy and the example family in the same commit, whichever lane asked for it.
The harness's settings for working in this repository.
Build settings every desktop project shares, the driver's and the modules' alike.
